appearance_facts.fact: The map uses a color scale where dark red/maroon shades represent lower values and pale yellow represents higher values, as indicated by the legend.
Pennsylvania (PA) is shaded in a dark maroon color, which corresponds to the lower end of the prevalence scale.
New Jersey (NJ) is shaded in a pale yellow color, which corresponds to the upper end of the prevalence scale.
Delaware (DE) is shaded in a light orange color, which corresponds to a mid-range value on the prevalence scale.
States like Florida (FL), Tennessee (TN), and Michigan (MI) are also shaded in pale yellow, similar to New Jersey.

printed_facts.fact: Prevalence of Species Z in US States
The 'High' end of the scale is pale yellow (100) and the 'Low' end is dark maroon (0).
PA (Pennsylvania) is labeled in the northeast region.
NJ (New Jersey) is labeled in the mid-Atlantic region.
DE (Delaware) is labeled in the mid-Atlantic region.

public_definitions: The goal is to open the state prevalence record that should be routed into the highest-prevalence priority follow-up workflow.
The routing criterion is the 'Highest prevalence state in the dashboard'.
